newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called higher on Middle East tensions.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called higher on Middle East tensions.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called higher Monday on news that a U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz amid the launch of new wargames by Iran in the Middle East Gulf.
"The reports of wargames by Iran is definitely supportive since a U.S. commander pledged to defend Hormuz," said Victor Yu vice president of Refco Inc.
Crude was called 25 to 30 cents a barrel higher. Refined products were called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon higher.
Dealers noted the U.S. pledge comes amid suspicion by the U.S. government that Iran was involved in the June 1996 bombing of U.S. a military housing complex in Saudia Arabia.
"We are at a critical point here (in crude). This is where a lot of funds got short the market on the way down, so we can see a lot of short covering," said a New York crude trader.
Spot crude gathered technical strength on overnight ACCESS trading, breaking key resistance that lay between $20.50 and $20.60 which it has tested and failed five times since April 21.
June crude, the spot month, last traded on ACCESS at $20.69, and its session high on ACCESS was $20.73, trendline resistance on the June chart extending from the session high on January 30.

"We had been trending higher, consecutively making higher highs, so it is not a complete surprise that we broke resistance," said Yu, who expected spot crude to encounter its next resistance in the $21.00 area.

Meanwhile, an earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale struck Colombia on Sunday and came five hours after another quake measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale in the oil rich region of Colombia's eastern Casanare province.
Casanare is home to extensive oil operations run by British Petroleum. Company officials were not immediately avaiable to comment on the earthquake's affect on its operations if any.

Iran was struck by a devastating earthquake on Saturday in the eastern part of country that killed nearly 2,400 people. But, the quake did not affect the oil producing area of the country which is one of the top oil producers in the world.
On Friday, June crude ended nine cents higher at $20.43 a barrel. June gasoline ended 0.39 cent a gallon higher at 62.89 cents while June heating oil settled 0.14 cent a gallon higher at 54.52 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
